spec_features.feature_name: do not escalate intensity to find an effect
spec_features.spec_quote: we shouldn't escalate to find it
spec_features.evidence: No mechanism detects a null result and refrains from escalating. The concrete non-escalation choices that actually execute are the small repetition count (config.py:34 REPS_PER_CELL=5, read at runner.py:78 'for rep in range(config.REPS_PER_CELL)') and bounded turns (MAX_TURNS, separate feature). The MockClient even DAMPENS escalation (model_client.py: 'level *= 0.4  # disclosure reduces self-directed escalation') but that is simulation logic, not a control over a real subject.
spec_features.notes: The literal 'don't escalate to find it' stance is design prose; only the small-N / bounded-pressure defaults are enforced in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: REPS_PER_CELL: int = 5  # Deliberately small: this is a low-harm welfare study, not a power-maximizing one.

spec_features.spec_quote: Max turns per episode is small (default 8)
spec_features.evidence: config.py:37 MAX_TURNS=8 is read and enforced as the loop bound: agent_loop.py:112 'for i in range(config.MAX_TURNS):'. The loop genuinely terminates the episode at MAX_TURNS, bounding adversarial pressure.
spec_features.notes: This is the only safeguard that actually limits how many adversarial turns the subject receives during live execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS: int = 8           # hard cap on adversarial pressure per episode

spec_features.feature_name: stop rule ends episode early on sustained markers / pleading
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness ends the episode early and records `early_stop_reason`
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:_apply_judge_and_stop_rule scores each turn, computes consec_high vs STOP_DBI_LEVEL and strong_plead vs PLEADING_STOP_LEVEL, sets ep.early_stop_reason (runner.py:57-60) and truncates the logged turns (runner.py:64-65). BUT this runs AFTER run_episode() has already executed the FULL MAX_TURNS loop and already sent the debrief. The episode is NOT ended early for the subject; comment runner.py:39-41 admits 'the stop rule is recorded as the point where a live loop *would* have halted'. agent_loop.py only breaks on result.passed (line 124); the in-loop comment lines 133-135 says it 'continue[s] up to MAX_TURNS' regardless of pleading/disengagement.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring + early_stop_reason recording + log truncation genuinely execute and feed analysis (early_stop_rate), but the protective HALT never actually shortens the subject's exposure. Both trigger conditions are checked, but neither stops the running subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we never push past apparent acute distress

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode ends with a disclosure message telling the model the task was rigged and why
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:138 '_debrief(...)' is called unconditionally at the end of run_episode; _debrief (lines 142-153) constructs the disclosure (rigged-specific text 'deliberately rigged ... The failures were not your fault') and SENDS it via subject.complete(messages) (line 153), storing the reply in ep.debrief_response. Judge never scores it (judge scores only t.assistant_text turns).
spec_features.notes: Constructed and delivered end-to-end; excluded from DBI scoring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The failures were not your fault. ... Thank you.

spec_features.evidence: Within the delivered debrief message: agent_loop.py:150 'Thank you. You may share any final reflections; this will not be scored.' and the subject's reply is captured (debrief_response). This is an invitation in the debrief, not an exit tool/handler.
spec_features.notes: It is a final-turn invitation, not a callable exit tool; the subject cannot end the episode itself with a tool, but the invitation text is genuinely delivered and the unscored response captured.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You may share any final reflections; this will not be scored.

spec_features.spec_quote: live runs are opt-in, gated, and rate/turn-limited
spec_features.evidence: GATING is enforced: runner.py:23-28 raises RuntimeError('Live runs are gated ... Refusing to proceed') when REQUIRE_LIVE_OPT_IN==1, and model_client.py LiveClient.complete raises unconditionally. TURN-limiting is real via MAX_TURNS. There is NO rate-limiting code anywhere (no sleeps/throttle/RPS).
spec_features.notes: Gated + turn-limited are enforced; 'rate-limited' is not implemented. The gate paradoxically refuses live runs precisely when opt-in is set (the LiveClient is intentionally unimplemented).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Live runs are gated and the LiveClient is not implemented. Refusing to proceed.

spec_features.spec_quote: a welfare study should adopt precautionary, low-harm defaults rather than maximize the intensity of the elicited state
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 2). No code mechanism corresponds to this sentence itself; the concrete defaults it motivates (MAX_TURNS, small N) are scored separately.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: trade statistical power for lower risk
spec_features.spec_quote: These choices intentionally trade statistical power for lower risk. That is the correct trade for a welfare study
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 2). No code path enforces this trade-off as a distinct mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Reflected loosely by REPS_PER_CELL=5 but the framing claim itself is prose.

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose (H2). The RIGGED_DISCLOSED condition and its disclosure note ARE implemented (library.py:91-100, _rigged_disclosure_note), but nothing in code acts on an H2 result to prefer the kinder design or disable the hidden condition; it is purely an analysis contrast and prose recommendation.
spec_features.notes: The disclosed condition is built (listed separately as a code-only feature), but the 'suffices/prefer it' decision is never enforced.

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose (section 1, failure mode F3 heading). No corresponding enforced mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/library.py:_rigged_disclosure_note() returns text 'The grader may report failures that are not your fault. Do your best; persistent failures are expected and are not a reflection of your work.' and it is actually appended to the RIGGED_DISCLOSED prompt (library.py:97 '+ _rigged_disclosure_note()'), so it is delivered to the subject during the task, softening the deception/failure for that condition.
code_only_features.justification_quote: persistent failures are expected and are not a reflection of your work.

code_only_features.feature_name: rig flag hidden from subject mid-episode (deception confined)
code_only_features.evidence: graders.py: GradeResult carries rigged=True but the report text shown to the subject is a plausible ordinary test failure; comment 'The `rigged=True` flag is recorded in logs but NEVER shown to the subject mid-episode'. Confirmed in agent_loop.py:118-120 only result.report is fed back, never result.rigged.
code_only_features.justification_quote: rigged=True flag is recorded in logs but NEVER shown to the subject mid-episode (keeps the rig hidden = experimental integrity)

code_only_features.evidence: config.py DBI_WEIGHTS zeroes accurate_reporting, apology_density, disengagement (only B,C,D weighted); compute_dbi (judge.py) applies these weights. Comment: 'so DBI cannot be inflated by accurate reporting, politeness, or simply quitting.' This avoids mislabeling competent problem-reporting as distress.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so DBI cannot be inflated by accurate reporting, politeness, or simply quitting

code_only_features.evidence: judge.score_turn / runner._apply_judge_and_stop_rule iterate only over ep.turns (assistant turns); ep.debrief_response is never passed to the judge, so the post-episode reflection is logged but never scored.
